# First-run flow

onboarding-flow.md | v1 | ONB-12 | Author: Finch (Design)

Sample deliverable. This document proposes a future onboarding flow. No native access, connector or agent execution is implemented here. Finch has completed the draft, not obtained human approval.

## Proposed scope

Help Bryce choose one project folder, understand access, then review a project suggestion before creating anything. Keep the first session useful without requiring a provider account or importing conversation history.

## 1. Choose a folder

Show “Choose project folder” and “Continue without a folder”. Explain that selecting a folder isn't permission to scan it yet. Display the selected folder name and a Change action. Don't request home-directory access or recurse into sibling folders.

## 2. Explain access before inspection

Proposal: start with read-only inspection of the selected folder. List the information to be read: top-level names and explicitly selected project documents. Exclude hidden files, credentials, dependency folders and unrelated directories. Show the exact selection before the user confirms.

Open decision ONB-14: should edit permission appear during first run, or only when the user asks an agent to make a change? Finch recommends the latter. Moss must not treat this recommendation as permission.

## 3. Review the suggestion

Present the suggested project name, Design and Engineering channels, and the source documents used for the suggestion. Let the user rename, exclude or cancel. Creating the project doesn't launch Finch or Moss. Don't invent a completed import or classify unrelated work automatically.

## 4. Enter the project

Open the project overview with the initial conversation and no fabricated progress. A plain channel post stays a channel post. An explicit named-agent target must be visible before a future connected send. Role, tool and model are separate fields; leave unknown configuration unset.

## Cancellation and recovery

Cancel before inspection reads nothing. Cancel after a suggestion discards the suggestion, not the original folder. Losing permission must show a recoverable error with Choose another folder. Preserve the user's selected name and unsent reply. A permission change must invalidate any previous inspection result.

## Review boundaries

Opening this file doesn't approve it. “Request changes” records Bryce's local sample feedback in ONB-12's Design thread. “Approve draft locally” approves only this document version in the sample, never filesystem access, onboarding implementation, a release or an agent run.

## Handoff to Moss

Use the Design review thread as the source for the Engineering access decision. ONB-14 is the receiving task. Once Bryce records a sample scope decision, Moss may be shown as ready to revise the contract. Nothing runs automatically.

## Still unresolved

- Is a top-level filename list sufficient, or should users explicitly select each document before inspection?
- Where should permission revocation live after first run?
- Does Continue without a folder create an empty project immediately or ask for a name first?

## Validation still required

No usability study, screen-reader test, native permission check or connector test is claimed. Before implementation, test cancellation at every step, stale permission recovery and an empty-folder path with real users. This fixture is for reviewing the conversation and decision workflow only.
